prerequisites: Knowledge of Mathematics I and II from high school (Bachillerato científico-tecnológico), including elementary algebra, trigonometry, and basic calculus.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge on: linear algebra.
Utilize the basic properties of real and complex numbers and perform fundamental operations with them.
Use the basic elements of Linear Algebra: systems of linear equations, vector spaces and linear applications and use matrices to simplify their study.
Identify metric properties in vector spaces, through the dot product, norm, or distance.
Calculate eigenvalues and eigenvectors and diagonalize endomorphisms and matrices.
Solve geometric problems in the plane and in space.
Identify the basic elements of differential equations and systems of differential equations and use algebraic tools to solve elementary cases.

syllabus_topics: Topic 2. Systems of linear equations and matrices.
2.2. Solving systems using the Gauss Method. Application to inverse matrix calculation.
3.2. Linear combinations and linear independence. Bases and dimension. Coordinates.
4.3. Kernel and image of an application. Classification of linear applications.
5.3. Applications to solving systems of linear differential equations.
6.1. Euclidean vector space. Scalar product and metric properties.
2. Matrix calculation and systems of equations
3. Vector spaces and changes of basis
assessment_rules: The final grade (NF) is calculated as: NF = 0.15*NL + maximum (0.15*NA + 0.7*NC, 0.85*NC), where NL is the laboratory practice grade, NA is the classroom practice grade, and NC is the average grade of the written controls, all out of 10 points. To pass, students must obtain at least 2.5 points out of 10 in each of the partial controls. If this minimum is not met in any control, the final grade will be a fail, and the numerical grade on the transcript will be the minimum of NF and 4.5. In extraordinary calls, a written exam with two parts and a laboratory practice test will be conducted, using the same evaluation formula as in the ordinary call. For differentiated evaluation, if classroom attendance is not possible, the final grade is NF = 0.15*NL + 0.85*NC, with passing requiring NF >= 5, NL >= 2.5, and NC >= 2.5 in each written exam part.
